To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel splice site variant of CFH that causes aHUS and that the variant is pathogenic.

a paternally inherited novel heterozygosity splice site variant c.3134- 2A>G in CFH results in an in-frame deletion of 9 amino acid residues in the SCR 17 and 19 of CFH, which is assumed essential for proper protein function and leads to uncontrolled complement activation.
a novel heterozygously inherited splice site variant in CFH leads to an in-frame deletion of 9 amino acid residues in SCR domains 17 and18, and is associated with the manifestation of aHUS.

the identification, characterization and application of the novel splice variant in the CFHI gene.
the development of novel, more efficient methods for the analysis of genetic data and its application in clinical practice.
the identification, functional characterization, and clinical relevance of pathogenic variants in the genes involved in the complement pathway.
